album: The Piano in the Room and the Blues
excerpt: This collection of intimate piano solos was issued on Mike Westbrook's 90th birthday, just prior to his passing, giving the eleven pieces an aura of famous last words, even though they were uttered twenty years ago. Additionally, solo playing was tertiary to Westbrook's legacy, overshadowed by 60 years of breakthrough long-form works like Marching Song and The Cortège, the community outreach of the Brass Band, and a slew of durable recordings by mid-sized and large ensembles.

This New World CD is by my count the fourth or fifth edition in half a century of a record that should never go out of print. Julius Hemphill released it on LP soon after its 1972 recording on his Mbari label. (Its name is writ large on the original cover; his own name did not appear. New World adds it to the facsimile cover.) He distributed it himself, and not many copies circulated.
